sample_unit: patients with diabetes (nearly one million) in the Andalusian Population Health Database

links.outcome: Sex-stratified bias in synthetic data versus real data not visible in standard metrics
links.effect: Bias and domain-specific sex-stratified analyses reveal inconsistencies not discernible through standard metrics, despite comparable aggregate predictive performance.
links.quote: However, bias and domain-specific sex-stratified analyses reveal inconsistencies not discernible through standard metrics, while data augmentation provides no performance benefit, as data saturation is reached given the large source population.

unlisted_practices: Using synthetic data generated by adversarial autoencoders to train clinical prediction models while preserving privacy
Combining machine learning utility metrics with domain-specific biomedical plausibility evaluation to validate synthetic data

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates a generative model for longitudinal synthetic patient data generation, testing its utility, bias (sex-stratified analyses), and clinical fidelity against real-world data for risk prediction.

primary.practice: synthetic data validation framework and bias evaluation
